title: Predictive scaling window desync causes reserved-pool shortfalls and customer 5xxs
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Summary: During coordinated morning traffic spikes we observed repeated reserved-pool shortfalls for several enterprise tenants (notably NimbusPay and ArbourRetail) that triggered customer-facing 5xx errors and increased latency. Investigation indicates a desynchronization between the predictive autoscaler windowing logic (controller) and the allocator's traffic smoothing/decay function, which resulted in under-provisioned reserved pools for short, high-amplitude bursts. This ticket tracks the bugfix, mitigations, communications, and follow-up hardening work.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a dedicated tenant with reserved pool enabled and burst credits configured.
2) Replay a synthetic traffic pattern: 3x baseline QPS for 90s, 1.2x for 10s, then drop to baseline. Repeat on 3-minute cadence.

3) Observe autoscaler telemetry: controller predicts required headroom but allocator's decay reduces effective headroom quickly; pool size fails to increase fast enough leading to allocation rejections and 5xx gateway errors.
4) Reproduce across two regions to validate cross-region policy interactions.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers experienced degraded availability during morning peak windows for ~2 hours across two regions. Error rates spiked to 6-8% for affected routes and some customers reported production incidents. Business impact includes SLA breaches for higher-tier customers and an open escalation with NimbusPay SRE team.
root_cause_summary: The predictive autoscaler (controller) and pool allocator use different smoothing/decay implementations and window alignment. Controller forecasts over a 60s lookahead using exponential smoothing with alpha=0.25 anchored on wall-clock buckets; allocator applies a separate decay factor and a 90s effective smoothing that trims recently observed surge signal earlier than the controller expected. During short, high-amplitude bursts the allocator's aggressive decay caused available headroom to be lower than the controller's planned allocation, leading to delayed or insufficient scale-ups. Edge condition: burst-credit accounting also misaligned by one evaluation tick, allowing bursts to exceed intended limits for a few seconds which downstreamed into allocation churn.
mitigation: Short-term: rolled out a cluster-level feature flag disabling allocator aggressive decay for affected regions and applied a conservative safety buffer (+15% headroom) to predictive allocations for enterprise-tier tenants. Communications: notified impacted customers with NRT incident updates and offered 1:1 postmortem. Medium-term: align smoothing windows and source-of-truth for burst-credit consumption between controller and allocator and add a fast-path preemptive scale-up for >2x baseline sustained >30s.
timeline: 2025-11-04 06:42 UTC: Pager triggered - spikes observed in us-west-2 for reserved pools. NimbusPay SRE reached out via support channel.
2025-11-04 07:10 UTC: Initial mitigation - enabled safety buffer via runtime config for affected tenants; immediate error rate reduced but not fully resolved.
2025-11-04 09:30 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis formed: smoothing/window mismatch between controller and allocator.
2025-11-05 13:00 UTC: Hotfix PR submitted that aligns decay math to controller's exponential smoothing and adds a one-evaluation tick headroom reserve.
2025-11-06 02:00 UTC: Hotfix deployed to canary clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; observed 90% reduction in allocation rejections.
2025-11-08 21:15 UTC: Stakeholder review: PM and Reliability approved rollout to remaining regions with gradual ramp.
2025-11-12 10:00 UTC: Rollout to all regions in progress; monitoring shows stable headroom for 72h window.
next_steps: 1) Merge allocator/controller smoothing alignment into stable branch and monitor for regression for 7 days.
2) Implement explicit source-of-truth for burst-credit accounting and add cross-checking telemetry between controller and allocator.
3) Add unit and property tests that simulate sub-2m burst patterns and assert no allocation rejections.
4) Postmortem with NimbusPay and update runbook to include this class of desync.
decision_log: 2025-11-05: Decided to prioritize correctness of smoothing math over micro-optimizations that shave latency; safety buffer accepted as interim tradeoff.
2025-11-06: Chose staged rollout with canary -> regional -> global to limit blast radius.
2025-11-10: Agreed to add a focused E2E test harness for burst scenarios in CI.
